text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has asked the ministry of defence to get army's help to rid illicit weapons and drug trafficking menace.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said she was avoiding confrontation with present government in order to give it full opportunity to work.
- The driver of the Zulfikar Express, that crashed near Khanewal on Monday, told an inquiry team that he is medically unfit to perform night duty, but his boss did not care and ordered to him on.
- Former Afghan premier Gulbuddin Hekmatyar has urged Pakistan to review its "support to a particular group" and work towards resolving the Afghan crisis.
- The trial of Asif Ali Zardari, husband of Benazir Bhutto, and 18 police and intelligence officers accused of killing Murtaza Bhutto opens inside the Karachi jail on Thursday, court sources said.
- The government is considering to ban militant sectarian organisations -- Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan and Sipah-i-Mohammad -- to contain sectarian terrorism, a source said.
- The government has decided to hike power tariffs by two percent every month without making any official announcement to the effect.
- The government has decided to prepare a 15-year perspective plan to be launched in 1998.
- The Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) has a confirmed order to supply 36,000 tonnes of long grain Irri-6 white rice to Mauritius, TCP sources said.
- The Pakistan International Airlines has won a contract to supply food to the British Airways.
- The government will re-negotiate agreements with the sponsors of private sector thermal power projects to cap prices of electricity at a "mutually agreeable" level.
- A three-member delegation of the International Monetary Fund arrived in Islamabad for a review of country's economy.
- Hinopak Motors Ltd has registered a 224 percent rise in pre-tax profit in the first half of current fiscal year (July-December 1996)
- Terming debt retirement as government's key priority, Chairman Privatisation Commission Khwaja Asif emphasized to accelerte pace of privatisation.
